title: ANZIIF confirms Summit lineup, unveils Discovery Hub for Sydney event
full_text:
With fewer than 100 days to go, the Australian and New Zealand Institute of Insurance and Finance (ANZIIF) has confirmed the full speaker lineup for its inaugural International Insurance Summit and announced a new central networking space, the Discovery Hub.
The two-day event will take place at ICC Sydney on February 11-12, 2027. ANZIIF describes it as its biggest event yet, bringing insurance professionals from around the globe together. Earlier Insurance Business reporting said more than 900 delegates were expected. For brokers, the program is built to connect the latest thinking with decisions facing the industry now.
Holly Ransom will serve as MC. International keynote speakers Jerry Michalski and April Rinne are joined by Future Crunch founder Tane Hunter and change strategist Michael McQueen. ANZIIF said their sessions will challenge delegates to rethink AI, the future of work, leadership and how to thrive in constant uncertainty.
Michalski, founder of Open Global Mind, has advised corporations on AI deployment. Rinne, a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader, advises organisations including Airbnb, Nike and the World Bank on workforce and demographic change. Ransom is chief executive of Emergent Global and has hosted events across more than 25 countries.
Industry speakers include ANZ chief economist Richard Yetsenga, geopolitical strategist Dr. Merriden Varrall, Munich Re managing director Scott Hawkins and Insurtech Australia CEO Simone Dossetor.
Read more: ANZIIF reveals four-stream program for inaugural International Summit
The program runs across four streams: Macro, Technology, Innovation and Resilience. Delegates can tailor their experience across issues from geopolitical instability and climate risk to AI deployment, emerging liabilities and workforce capability.
Those themes track pressures already facing the market. In April 2026, the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority called for a step-change in how insurers, banks and super trustees manage AI-related risks. The Insurance Council of Australia’s September 2025 submission to the Productivity Commission said 90% of insurance employers were experiencing a skills shortage and nearly 30% of the workforce is expected to reach retirement age by 2030.
For brokers advising clients on emerging risks and managing their own talent pipelines, the sessions offer a chance to test those issues against local and international views. ANZIIF’s Summit portal lists up to 11 CIP points for attending.
The Discovery Hub will be a dedicated, central meeting place bringing delegates, exhibitors and partners together for networking, conversation and collaboration. Open across both days, it is intended to give the ideas raised on stage somewhere to keep developing. Earlier reporting said 60 marketplace exhibitors were expected. ANZIIF said further details will be announced.
ANZIIF CEO Katrina Shanks (pictured) said the Summit offers a chance to step back, look ahead and reconnect.
“We’re bringing an extraordinary mix of people and ideas together, and I can’t wait to welcome our industry to Sydney,” Shanks said. “Come with your leadership team and emerging leaders and leave with fresh perspectives, practical ideas and connections to help you move forward.”

Munich Re managing director Scott Hawkins said the program’s combination of international perspective and local industry focus made it a worthwhile use of time for market practitioners.
ANZIIF said further speaker commentary will be available through the Summit portal ahead of the event.
ANZIIF encourages professionals and teams to reserve their places now. Team bookings can get underway without every attendee being confirmed, and tickets can be booked through the Summit portal.
